The petitioner is facing trial for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506, 114 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The grievance of the petitioner is that these proceedings are pending since 2011 and therefore, is seeking for an appropriate direction to expedite the matter and conclude the trial.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
3. On examining the records, it is noticed that the trial is pending for almost 12 years for an offence punishable under Section 498A.
Therefore, I am of the view that this is a fit case, by exercising inherent jurisdiction, an appropriate direction needs to be given to decide the case as expeditiously as possible.
opennyai_summary.1_June_2023__decision:
4. Hence, I pass the following:

(iii) The learned Judge shall ensure that the complainant and the prosecution will not seek adjournments and protract the conclusion of the trial.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The petitioners are before this Court calling in question the registration of a crime in Crime No.0084/2023 registered for offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 504 read with Section 34 of the IPC and under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The parties to the lis were also before the Family Court in M.C.No.3238/2023 and have settled the dispute NC: 2024:KHC:45847 amongst themselves before the Family Court by terms of settlement.
I. The Petitioner has filed this petition against the Respondent under Section 13 (1)
(i-a) (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for the relief of dissolution of his marriage with the respondent.
In the course of Mediation, the parties along with their respective advocates participated in the mediation and
Their marriage was solemnized on 15.02.2019 at the residence of bride, House No.256, V V Nagar,
Vasanthpur, Bengaluru 560 061 as per Hindu rites and customs.
Subsequently the said marriage was registered on 09.10.2019 before the Registrar of Marriage,
Bagalkot vide Marriage Registration Number: BGK-HM250-2019- 2020 and stored in CD Number: BGKM13.
2.
The petitioner and the respondent state and admit that due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, they did not have any compatible marital relationship between them and they are separated since May 2020.
The respondent has lodged a complaint before East Zone Women Police Station, Shivajinagar,
Bengaluru against the petitioner and his family member for the offence punishable under section 498A of and 34 of IPC read with section 3 & 4 DP Act., the same in Crime No.0084/2023 pending on the file of VI ACJM., Bengaluru, in view of settlement arrived herein the respondent has agreed to co-operate with the petitioner and his family members for closure/disposal/quashing of aforesaid Crime No.0084/2023.
7.
Both the petitioner and the respondent agree that they have already exchanged their respective valuables, articles and other belongings.

The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs. 14,00,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Only) towards maintenance, education, medical and other incidental expenses for the child, the petitioner is paying a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Only) in the name of the child Hardhik by way of demand draft bearing No. 681635 dated 29.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, Gottigere Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent before this Hon'ble Court while reporting settlement.
Further the petitioner has agreed to pay balance a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-
(Rupees Four Lakhs Only) to the respondent by way of demand draft bearing No. 681636 dated 29.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, Gottigere Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a criminal petition intended to be filed by the petitioner.
6.
9. The petitioner and the respondent hereby withdraw all the allegations made against each other in the petition or otherwise.
The petitioner and the respondent hereby declare that they shall have no claim of any nature whatsoever against each other either past, present or future.
11. The petitioner and the respondent herein state that there is no undue influence, force, or coercion in entering into this agreement from any one or any thing.
12. The petitioner and the respondent admit that they shall not Interfere in each other's lives in future.
III. In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, the parties pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to dissolve the marriage solemnized on 15.02.2019 at the residence of bride, House No.256, V V Nagar, Vasanthpur, Bengaluru 560 061 and for cancellation of marriage certificate registered on 09.10.2019 before the Registrar of Marriage, Bagalkot vide Marriage Registration Number: BGK-HM250- 2019- 2020 and stored in CD Number: BGKM13 by granting a decree of divorce in terms of the agreement.
IV. The parties will appear on 04.09.2024 before the Hon'ble court for passing orders in terms of the agreement."
4.
Therefore, in light of the settlement arrived at between the parties quoted supra, I deem it appropriate to terminate the proceedings pending against these petitioners in the subject petition.
For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER i. Criminal Petition is disposed.
